To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) non-random missing data have a significant impact on the quality of collaborative filtering predictions and rankings, (2) the impact of nonrandom missing data can be mitigated with a simple, easy to implement, and effective method, and (3) the impact of missing data on collaborative filtering predictions and recommendations is not limited to the Netflix Prize data, but is also observed with data from the Movielens and Epinions recommender systems.
non-random missing data can have a significant negative effect on collaborative prediction, but a positive effect on collaborative ranking.

(a) non-random missing data have a strong effect on collaborative prediction, (b) non-random missing ratings have a stronger effect on collaborative prediction than non-random implicit feedback, (c) non-random missing feedback has a strong effect on the performance of collaborative ranking, and (d) non-random missing implicit feedback has a stronger effect on ranking performance than non-random missing ratings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of non-ignorable missing data on collaborative filtering and collaborative ranking.
the impact of non random missing data on the performance of collaborative prediction and ranking.
the question of how to best use the observed ratings in order to predict the missing ratings, and how to best use both the observed and missing ratings in order to rank the items.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

non-random missing data can be very detrimental to the quality of collaborative prediction, but that the impact on collaborative ranking is more complex and depends strongly on the type and extent of the missing data.
non-random missingness can lead to significant performance degradation, especially for top-ranked items, and that it is important to take missing data into account.
the impact on prediction accuracy is small, but the effect on ranking accuracy is significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
non-random missing data has a significant impact on collaborative prediction and ranking.
, when missingness is not random, the performance of recommender systems is severely degraded.
non-random missing data can lead both to biased parameter estimation, and to biased prediction, even when the missing data are ignorable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of nonrandom missing data on collaborative filtering is significant, and must be taken into account in the design of collaborative filtering systems.
recommender systems that do not account for non-random missing data may be biased, and this bias can be substantial.
recommender systems should not make strong assumptions about the observation process.
